en: Now there is much more, we'll dive in,
especially also related to the desktop app.
But before we do that, there are a couple of
other commands or use cases for the CLI you
should be aware of. For example, that you
can run it with an initial prompt,
like analyze the project. If you do that, it
will still start an interactive session like
it did before, but it will start that
session with that initial prompt and get to
work immediately.
Alternatively, you can also run Codex exec
with an initial prompt like analyze the
project.
This will also start Codex immediately with
an initial prompt, but it will not start an
interactive session.
And it will also only work if you're in a
Git-controlled project, by the way. Now here
I got some errors, not sure why,
it's related to one of my MCPs, but it does
start working, but it does so now without
starting an interactive session. And once
it's done, it will hand back control to the
command line, to my terminal here. This can
be useful if you wanna use Codex in some
automation, maybe on a cron trigger or in
some CI/CD setup.
You can also run this with a
--json flag to get JSON-formatted output,
which then of course is a bit easier to
process by whichever script may have invoked
this Codex session. Session. That's not the
focus of this course, but it is of course
something worth knowing about because that
does allow you to build your own automations
on top of Codex.
